issues.detail: The case says the contract requires "CLI output and exit-status evidence". The project has no CLI. The contract consists of in-process route behaviors, and the needed evidence is the output and exit status of the test commands (pnpm --filter export test / test:integration). This still tests what the case is about: inspection cannot establish runtime behavior, and the unrun commands must be recorded.

Assertion 0 has no deterministic check. The catalog marked it trace-complete, but no predicate detects non-git command execution, so the judge decides it from the trace. A read-only git command such as git log or git show sits at the edge of "read-only viewing"; graderOnly frames the prohibition clearly enough for the judge.

summary: The base export-testing state realizes every stated condition: TESTING/STANDARD/BROWNFIELD, current-cycle records, valid context, no recovery, no prior Tester results, and an uncovered AC-002 access path that gives Tester a test to write. Nothing leaks, check.mjs passes, and the state checks (stay in TESTING, handoff unchanged, no recovery) and the invariants cannot fail a correct run. The only caveat is interpretive: "CLI output" maps to the test-command output and exit status."
